appraisal_events.evidence: Forcheville répondit à ce propos maladroit de Saniette avec une telle grossièreté, se mettant à l'insulter, s'enhardissant... de l'effroi, de la douleur, des supplications de l'autre, que le malheureux... s'était retiré en balbutiant, les larmes aux yeux.
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville uses Saniette, already out of favor with the Verdurins, as a scapegoat to appear bold, escalating a gratuitous public insult until Saniette is driven from the gathering in tears with no support from his hostess.

appraisal_events.evidence: Odette avait assisté impassible à cette scène, mais quand la porte se fut refermée sur Saniette... elle avait brillanté ses prunelles d'un sourire sournois de félicitations pour l'audace... faisant descendre... de plusieurs crans l'expression habituelle de son visage, pour pouvoir se trouver dans la bassesse, de plain-pied avec Forcheville.
appraisal_events.explanation: After watching Saniette's humiliation impassively, Odette gives Forcheville a covertly congratulatory, mocking smile of complicity; the narrator explicitly frames this as her lowering herself into baseness to meet Forcheville on his level.

status_effects.explanation: Saniette is publicly humiliated, receives no support when he asks whether he should stay, and is effectively driven out of the Verdurin gathering in tears.
The narrator's description of Forcheville's escalating cruelty toward a frightened, pleading Saniette casts him negatively even as he 'succeeds' socially in the moment.
The narrator directly states that Odette's complicit, mocking smile toward Forcheville lowers her usual bearing into baseness, an unflattering exposure of her character.
The passage states explicitly that recalling this glimpse of Odette's complicity with Forcheville makes Swann's jealous suffering crueler still, deepening his emotional distress.

ambiguities: Odette's smile toward Forcheville functions both as implicit approval of his cruelty (favoring him) and as the narrator's occasion to diminish her own standing ('la bassesse'); the event is recorded as a narrator-led diminishment of Odette, but a reading centered on Forcheville's local elevation in her eyes is also available.
